keystore.description: Release signing. The passwords come from $TANGO_ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD and $TANGO_ANDROID_KEY_PASSWORD (default: the keystore password).

AndroidIcon.description: AndroidIcon is the adaptive launcher icon (API 26+). Layers are 108 dp squares of which the launcher shows the centre 72 dp (the inner 66 dp is always visible, whatever the mask).

background.description: Background is a PNG or a colour "#RRGGBB". Default: the colour of the master icon's border.

foreground.description: Foreground PNG with transparency, ideally 432×432; keep the artwork inside the centre 66/108. Default: the master icon fitted to the visible 72 dp.

monochrome.description: Monochrome PNG for Android 13 themed icons (alpha only, same layout as Foreground). Default: none (themed icons are skipped).

DMGLayout.description: DMGLayout is the Finder window a disk image opens in. Sizes and positions are in points; positions are icon centres from the window's top left corner.

background.description: Background is a PNG, JPEG or TIFF drawn at the top left of the window at its size in points (a 72 dpi image: pixels; a file named x@2x.png next to x.png makes a Retina background).

title.description: volume name; default the app name

FileAssociation.description: FileAssociation registers the app for files with an extension.

name.description: shown by the system, e.g. "Markdown document"

Flatpak.description: Flatpak holds the settings of the Flatpak manifest.

finishArgs.description: FinishArgs are sandbox permissions added to the defaults (IPC, Wayland, X11 fallback, GPU, network), e.g. "--socket=pulseaudio" or "--filesystem=xdg-documents".

Frontend.description: Frontend says where the front end lives and how to run it.

dev.description: dev server command; its first printed http URL is used

devURL.description: dev server URL, when it cannot be read from the output

dist.description: build output, relative to Dir ("." when the sources are served as is)

install.description: run when Dir has package.json but no node_modules; default "npm install"

build.description: CFBundleVersion; default the version without its suffix

signIdentity.description: Device builds: the codesign identity (or $TANGO_IOS_SIGN_IDENTITY), the provisioning profile, and entitlements (default: the ones the profile grants).

usageDescriptions.description: UsageDescriptions overrides the text iOS shows when it asks for a permission, by permission name ("camera": "Scan receipts").

IOSIcons.description: IOSIcons are the iOS 18 appearance variants of the app icon (1024 PNG).

dark.description: dark appearance: artwork on a transparent or dark background

tinted.description: tinted appearance: grayscale artwork the system colours

Icons.description: Icons overrides the icon per platform. Every field is optional: what is not set is derived from Config.Icon, the master icon. The master icon is square artwork that fills the whole canvas (no transparent margin, no rounded corners), ideally 1024×1024 PNG. That is what iOS and Android expect, since they apply their own mask. Desktop systems expect the icon to carry its own shape, so tan derives one: a rounded square with the platform's margin and a soft shadow (macOS grid, also used for Windows and Linux). Give a platform its own file when the derived one is not good enough.

macos.description: MacOS is used as is: 1024×1024 PNG already in the macOS shape (the rounded square on an 824 px grid with transparent margin).

notification.description: Notification is the Android status-bar icon: white shapes on a transparent background (Android draws it as a mask), ideally 96×96. Without it push notifications use a white silhouette of the app icon.

windows.description: Windows is a PNG (shaped, transparent background; 256 px or more) or an .ico file used as is.

Installer.description: Installer is the "installer" section of tan.json: how tan package dresses its installers. Every field is optional. See docs/packaging.md.

Linux.description: Linux holds the settings of the Linux packages tan package makes with -format deb, rpm or flatpak. See docs/linux-packaging.md.

depends.description: Depends and RPMRequires are added to the defaults: GTK 3 and WebKitGTK 4.1, which the Tango runtime loads (libgtk-3-0 and libwebkit2gtk-4.1-0 for deb, their sonames for rpm).

description.description: Description: the first line is the one-line summary, the rest the long description. Default the app name.

maintainer.description: Maintainer is the Debian Maintainer and rpm Packager, "Name <email>".

package.description: Package is the deb and rpm package name; default the name in lower case with words joined by '-' ("My App" → "my-app").

app.description: PNG used instead of the derived shape

MacInstaller.description: MacInstaller customises the macOS disk image (package_dmg.go).

NSISInstaller.description: NSISInstaller customises the Windows NSIS installer (package_nsis.go).

desktopShortcut.description: DesktopShortcut is "ask" (default: a check box on the finish page), "always" or "never".

include.description: Include is an NSIS file included in the script; the macros it defines named customInit, customInstall and customUnInstall run in .onInit, at the end of the install section and at the start of the uninstall section.

languageDialog.description: LanguageDialog asks for the installer language at start; by default the installer follows the Windows display language.

license.description: License is a .txt or .rtf file shown on a licence page the user must accept.

runAfterInstall.description: RunAfterInstall offers "Run <app>" on the finish page; default true for a per-user installer, false for scope "machine" (an elevated installer). Turned on there, the app is started through Explorer so it does not inherit the installer's administrator token.

scope.description: Scope is "user" (default: %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs, HKCU, no UAC prompt, and the app can update itself) or "machine" (Program Files, HKLM, asks for administrator rights).

sidebarImage.description: SidebarImage is the welcome and finish pages' left image (164×314, .bmp, or .png that tan converts); HeaderImage the banner on the other pages (150×57). Default: NSIS's own.

template.description: Template is a Go text/template file that replaces the whole generated script (variables: docs/packaging.md).

welcome.description: Welcome shows the welcome page; default true.

Windows.description: Windows holds Windows-only settings. See docs/windows.md.

certificate.description: Code signing (tan sign, tan package): a PKCS#12 (.pfx) file, unless -cert or $TANGO_WINDOWS_CERT names another. The password is never read from tan.json: it comes from $TANGO_WINDOWS_CERT_PASSWORD.

publisher.description: Publisher is the certificate's subject, e.g. "CN=Example Ltd, O=Example Ltd, C=US"; MSIX packages need it (it must match the signing certificate).

description: Config is tan.json. Paths are relative to the project directory.

$schema.description: Schema is the URL of tan.json's JSON Schema, which editors use for completion and checks; tan ignores it.

appLinkPaths.description: AppLinkPaths limits AppLinks to these path prefixes ("/open/"); default every path.

appLinks.description: AppLinks are the web domains ("example.com", "*.example.com") whose https links open the app: iOS Universal Links (associated-domains entitlement) and Android App Links (autoVerify intent filters). The site proves the link with the files tan applinks writes (applinks.go).

fileAssociations.description: FileAssociations are the document types the app opens.

frontend.description: omit for a self-drawn UI app

icon.description: master icon: square, full-bleed PNG, ideally 1024×1024 (see Icons)

installer.description: Installer customises the installers tan package makes: the NSIS setup.exe and the macOS disk image. See docs/packaging.md.

localizations.description: Localizations are the languages the app declares to Apple platforms (CFBundleLocalizations); system-provided menu items and dialogs are localized only into these. Default: en, zh-Hans, zh-Hant, ja (the languages Tango's built-in strings ship).

name.description: display name; also names the executable (see Exe)

permissions.description: Permissions are the mobile capabilities the app uses ("camera", "location", ...; see permissions.go). tan build declares them: iOS usage descriptions in Info.plist, Android <uses-permission> entries.

urlSchemes.description: URLSchemes are the deep-link schemes the app opens (myapp for myapp://...); the app declares the same list in tango.Options.
